title: bug: the control-checkout follow gives up on a transient .git/index.lock, so a QA claim right after a landing can park the row with MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND
description:
Observed live on 2026-11-02 at 20:15:16Z, the first hour of worktree mode. qa-7328a40d's follow failed `git merge -q --ff-only` with "Unable to create '/mnt/d/projexts/moes/.git/index.lock': File exists". moe/control stayed at 7beed0bc, behind moe/work-2026-10-24 at 58c760f4. At 20:15:32Z the lock was gone, and a later follow had moved HEAD to 58c760f4. No row was parked this time.

Who uses the control checkout's index at the same time:
- the IDE: PyCharm's Windows git refreshes. Two Windows git processes were live at 20:15:32Z.
- peer wrappers: their follows, `git push refs/moe/board`, landings.

The defect:
- follow_control_checkout (scripts/moe-agent.sh, about line 6735) and its twin Invoke-MoeControlFollow (scripts/moe-agent.ps1, about line 6123) retry nothing on a lock error.
- They tolerate only one case: a peer's follow that held the lock and itself moved HEAD to the tip.
- The commit path already retries this: moe-agent.sh about :5081 ("5 x 2 s retry on index.lock"), and the ps1 twin about :5200-5209.

Why it matters: qa_control_preflight runs the follow, then qa_landed_gate checks that the claimed row's completion is in the control HEAD. If the follow lost a transient lock race for a row landed seconds earlier, the gate worktree_stops the seat with MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND and one report_blocked. That row has no blockedOnTaskIds, so it stays BLOCKED until a governor or human resets it. With about 8 coders landing and 3 QA seats claiming right after landings, that race is likely.

Fix, in both twins only: when the ff-only merge's stderr contains `index.lock`, re-check HEAD (keep the existing peer-moved-HEAD shortcut), sleep 2 s and retry. Use the same cap as the commit path, at most 5 tries. Every other failure path, and the final MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND alert after the last try, stays exactly as it is today. Never delete an index.lock.

Files: scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1, scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs. The existing 'lock' case (about :1238) must keep passing: a lock held throughout still ends in BEHIND, with the lock not deleted.
definitionOfDone: follow_control_checkout (sh) and Invoke-MoeControlFollow (ps1) retry the ff-only merge up to 5 times, 2 s apart, only when its error output contains index.lock. After each failed try they re-check whether HEAD already reached the tip.
A new postflight-worktree.cjs case passes under both postflight.sh and postflight.ps1: an index.lock that is released about 3 s into the follow ends with MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED and HEAD at the tip.
The existing 'lock' case still passes: a lock held for the whole retry window ends in MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND, and the lock file is never deleted.
Every other follow failure path (DIVERGED, the .moe-paths BEHIND, NOT_FOLLOWING) behaves as before and does not retry.
bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes. The verification command (bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh, plus the ps1 harness for the twin) exits 0 from the task worktree.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX scripts/moe-agent.sh follow_control_checkout, with the Edit tool. Anchor on the function, not on line numbers: peers in worktree mode move lines. Add `attempt` to its `local` line. Replace the block from `# The checked tip, not the ref:` through the MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED echo with:
    # The checked tip, not the ref: a target that moved since carries unchecked .moe paths.
    # A held .git/index.lock (the IDE's git, a peer's landing or follow) is retried like
    # index_refresh: at most 5 tries, 2 s apart. Any other failure is final. Never delete the lock.
    for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
        rc=0
        err=$(git -C "$MOE_TOP" -c core.hooksPath="$hooks" merge -q --ff-only --no-autostash "$tip" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
        new=$(git -C "$MOE_TOP" rev-parse -q --verify 'HEAD^{commit}' 2>/dev/null) || new=""
        [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || break
        # A peer's follow that held the index lock may already have moved HEAD to the tip.
        [ -n "$new" ] && git -C "$MOE_TOP" merge-base --is-ancestor "$tip" "$new" 2>/dev/null && return 0
        if [ "$attempt" -lt 5 ] && [[ "$err" == *index.lock* ]]; then sleep 2; continue; fi
        control_alert MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND "moe/control stays at $old, behind $target at $tip: ${err:0:1500}"; return 0
    done
    [ "$new" = "$old" ] || echo -e "${GREEN}[OK]${NC} MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED $old..$new"
Every try merges the same checked $tip, never a re-read target, and there is no sleep after the 5th try.
Error handling: every other failure keeps today's code, message and single attempt. That covers the local-edit and untracked refusals, plus the DIVERGED, .moe-paths BEHIND and NOT_FOLLOWING paths above, which return before the merge. The final BEHIND after a 5th lock failure is today's message. No new code or log line.
`bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` must pass. [[ ]] and for-in are already used in this file and parse under macOS /bin/bash 3.2.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented approved bounded loop exactly in follow_control_checkout: resets rc per try, rechecks HEAD, retries index.lock only, same checked tip, 4 sleeps max and unchanged final alert. bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && git diff --check exited 0. Existing function/file already at size threshold; localized loop follows approved structure.

Twin uses existing Invoke-MoeGit and Update-MoeSharedIndex retry shape; no new helper/dependency/log family. Loop stays inside existing try/finally; same checked tip and per-failure HEAD shortcut. ParseFile exited 0 under powershell.exe and pwsh.exe; BOM + LF byte assertions passed. Both wrappers' caller sites verified (preflight, QA follow, post-landing, loop top).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When the control-checkout follow's `git merge --ff-only` fails because .git/index.lock is held, both launcher twins re-check HEAD, then retry the same checked tip, up to 5 tries, 2 s apart. A lock that the IDE or a peer holds for a few seconds therefore no longer leaves moe/control behind, and a QA claim right after a landing passes its landed gate. A lock held for the whole window, and every other failure, ends exactly as today.
acceptanceCriteria: follow_control_checkout and Invoke-MoeControlFollow make at most 5 ff-only tries, 2 s apart, and retry only when the merge output contains index.lock; after each failed try they return quietly if HEAD already contains the tip.

wt-follow-lock 'released': a lock released about 3 s after the follow's first merge ends with exactly one MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED old..tip line and HEAD at the tip, on both postflight.sh and postflight.ps1.
wt-follow-lock 'held' and the existing follows 'lock' row: a lock held throughout ends in MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND after 5 tries per follow, and the lock file is not deleted.
wt-follow-lock 'other' and the existing follows rows: non-lock merge failures and the DIVERGED, .moe-paths BEHIND and NOT_FOLLOWING paths behave as before, with one try.
invariants: Never delete, reset, stash, force or clean: a refusal is still an alert and nothing moves
Every try merges the tip that the .moe-paths check already checked, never a re-read target ref
No new MOE_ code or log line, so the wrappers' code families stay identical and parity-check passes

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Hold the first merge with the existing WT_GIT_HOLD stub knob (as wtFollowRace does): rejected. On ps1, git.ps1 runs in-process (mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-git-stub), so the real git's lock stderr may never reach $m.Out, and the stub would sit on PATH for the whole launch. GIT_TRACE anchors the first merge with the real git and counts every try without changing the stub, which task-c7ca56e6 is also extending. 2) Add the try count to the existing 'lock' and 'edit' rows: rejected, because DoD 3 wants the existing 'lock' case unchanged; the cap and no-retry checks live in the new case instead. 3) A per-retry log line: rejected. Any new MOE_CONTROL_ code would change the wt-follow codes assertion for the 'lock' row, and the commit-path twin retries silently too. 4) A deterministic test of the in-loop HEAD re-check: not possible with today's stub. A merge whose HEAD already reached the tip exits 0 even with the lock held (probed, git 2.43), so the shortcut only matters between a failed merge and the next HEAD read; code review covers it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: follow_control_checkout is at scripts/moe-agent.sh ~:6701, with its merge at :6736. Its twin Invoke-MoeControlFollow is at scripts/moe-agent.ps1 ~:6083, with its merge at :6123 inside a try/finally that removes the temp hooks dir. The commit-path precedents are index_refresh (sh :5081, 5 tries with a sleep after every try) and Update-MoeSharedIndex (ps1 :5203). A worker launch runs the follow twice, at the loop top (:8614) and at the pre-flight switch (:3107), so the ratio assertions (merges equal to 5 or 1 times the [WARN] BEHIND lines) stay true whatever the number of follows. Only the follow passes --no-autostash; the W-side merge at sh :7062 and ps1 :6568 does not. launch() merges knobs into the wrapper env and puts the stub on PATH only for WT_GIT_* knobs; inherited scrubs GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR and GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, not GIT_TRACE. LIMIT is 180 s per launch, and the held scenario adds about 16 s.

Keep the hunks inside the follow blocks, the new function and one new registration line, so the rebase merges cleanly; a true conflict routes back as designed. Windows legs from WSL: use node.exe with a D: tmp and WSLENV for MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY. The full gate is about 50 min and needs set -m (scenario W) and env -i. On a very slow host, the second try can come after the 3 s release; the assertions only need at least 2 merges, so that is fine.
